Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates linear lucencies tracking along the mediastinal borders and extending into the neck, which is characteristic of pneumomediastinum caused by alveolar rupture (Macklin effect) rather than esophageal perforation or gastric issues. This pattern typically presents with air dissecting through the mediastinum, often more prominently anteriorly or along fascial planes, without the massive pleural effusion or hydropneumothorax seen in Boerhaave syndrome.
